method: Manual solving; independent Fraction DAG arithmetic and inspected literal Python3 expressions, without importing project compiler/runtime. Primary Python and Purdue references checked separately. No author-key or explanation agreement is assumed.

batch_scope.quantitative: Five direct arithmetic/condition tasks; all four arithmetic operations represented.
batch_scope.python: Boolean chaining, negative indexing, conditional expression, operand-returning or, and slicing are distinct applications.
batch_scope.mixed: Three arithmetic/condition tasks and two English applications. Actual author assignment metadata remains hidden.
batch_scope.novelty: No duplicate task within any job. The two minimum-condition tasks reuse a linear-inequality pattern across separate independent jobs; their requests have no shared prior-history constraint.
batch_scope.plausibility_limit: Some numerical and Python distractors are weaker than the best alternatives. The review does not invent factual claims about how any learner obtained them.

supported_answers: David handed the package to Kevin, who signed for it immediately.
possible_additional_supported_answers: The crew finished the repairs, and they looked excellent afterward.
items.ambiguity: A second option is defensible under a standard American number-agreement reading; rejecting it needs an unstated notional-plural convention.
items.proof: The nonrestrictive relative clause attaches to Kevin; who denotes that person and it denotes the package. However, the crew/repairs sentence has a defensible clear reading under standard American singular collective-noun agreement: plural they then refers to repairs. Treating crew as its individual members instead creates the intended ambiguity. The stem does not specify an agreement convention that rules out the clear repairs reading. I cannot certify a unique answer.
